01.title: Stressing the limit of sound perception
01.markdown:
**Stressing the limit of sound perception**

Sonic boundaries of sound and music recognition.

**1. Stressing #1: Timet music composition.** New Timet productions. Samples from:

- *LoLe – Musica leggiadra*, CD, I Dischi Forma, 2002/2003.
- *Compilatione*, CD, 2002.

**2. Stressing #2: multichannel pop songs** (stereo mp3 version of the original 5.1 mix). Samples from:

- *SRS Società Ritmico Sintetica*, from *Automated Mirrors, the Anthropical Forest*, DVD, 2003.

**3. Stressing #3: a cognitive exploration.** Physiological stress of sound perception and recognition. Excerpts from Timet musicians’ live processing sessions.

[Explore the examples](#excerpt)

02.title: Hyper Classicism
02.markdown:
**Timet perspectives on Classicism**

**1.** The idea of classicism refers to a cognitive public frame. We intend to criticise a static idea of musical heritage. We suggest an *ethic of using and abusing* cultural heritage. We also defend a sophisticated preservation of the *access to* and *availability of* all the original sources, at any level of processing.

**2. Memory as collective memory.** A dialectical, dynamic and truly electronic confrontation between music histories exemplifies the circle of *cultural synthesis*. Timet is against a strict, non-symbolic authors’-rights legislation.

See: *Easy Classics*, DVD. Cosottini, Brusci. Timet, 2002 (stereo mp3 version of the original 5.1 mix).

[Explore the examples](#excerpt)

03.title: State of immersion
03.markdown:
**Re-designing sound objects and spaces**

Designing *sonic objects* and *sound spaces*: towards a naturalisation of abstract sonic experiences. We create specific site conditions and produce specific sonic objects that give life, immediate expressive meaning and physicality to our electroacoustic compositions. Samples from:

- *L’ospite ingrato*, sound installation, Timet, 2003 (AC3 5.1 audio version; files available on request, [contact us](mailto:info@musi-co.com)). [Read](/archive/events/ospingr) · [Watch](#gallery-ospite)
- *Sonic objects*. Various designers and artists design objects for Timet, with Timet’s sound consultancy. [Gallery 01](#gallery-sound-obj) · [Gallery 02](#gallery-marble-obj)
- *Intersistema #1*, sound/dance installation, Sosta Palmizi–Timet, Fabbrica Europa 2003, Stazione Leopolda, 28–29 June. Stereo sample of the 8-channel live version. [Watch](#video-hic)

**Amplifying natural sites.** Hyper-exposing electroacoustic sound experiences inside relevant urban or natural sites. DVD audio-video productions. Samples from:

- *Marble. A matter of evidence*, DVD, installation, Timet, 2003 (AC3 audio files available on request, [contact us](mailto:info@musi-co.com); 5.1 audio version). [Watch](#gallery-marmo) Video directors: Reuven Halevi, Andrea Baldini, Letizia Renzini. 5.1 music composition by Timet.
- *Klangturm*, Expo.02, Biel. Live recordings and images (stereo mp3 version). Lorenzo Brusci directing and performing inside the Sound Tower; project by Andres Bosshard. [Watch](#gallery-klang)

04.title: Performative projects
04.markdown:
**Marble Cave Orchestra**

Featuring A. Bosshard (CH) – L. Brusci (IT) + Timet guests.

Immersive audio installation and concert for laptops, musicians and multichannel sound system.

“…the space will be filled with sound fantasies coming from multichannel recording sessions in a marble cave. Inside this natural reverberation chamber we apply our formal and sound-design research. Four sets: 1 – water / Bach; 2 – wind / Mozart; 3 – fire / Beethoven; 4 – ground / Schoenberg. Towards a sonic hybrid body.”

Acoustic musicians can be added as special guests; this must be requested and scheduled specifically. No audio technical requirements; only essential lighting support is needed.

05.title: Sonic architectures
05.markdown:
**Sonic architectures**

**We conceive a livable environment as an open process, in its synthetic, multiple and reversible evidence.** Any music aggregate is a symbol of a living process and expresses dynamic relationships among all its perceptual elements. From our perspective, a symbolic system is expressive (and logical) when it is deeply editable: editability makes any symbolic system dynamic and alive. Symbolic systems stand for possible environments.

**To free a complex music, integrated in a livable space.** Aesthetic contents are an alternative model of reality: a continuous symbolic world made of dynamic identities and of the reversibility of every state. Synchronicity and environment are context-interfaces between Man and Complexity.

- Ecology of a dynamic open space.
- Immaterial architecture.
- Multiplicity and habitat.

A nonlinear architecture. An active process. Example: *Virtual Gardens*, Giovanni Antignano. [Explore](#video-vg1test) (Flash animation; thanks to J. Tarbell for the source code).

**Sonic garden design**

- *Ri.Natura*. [Watch](/archive/events/rinatura) Documentation will be available soon.
- *Symbolic Walls*, Timet, 2004. Giovanni Antignano–Timet [Watch](#video-mould); Maurizio Meossi, Filippo Innocenti – SPIN [Watch](#gallery-symbolic-wall).

06.title: Metalanguages and nonlinearity
06.markdown:
**Metalanguages and nonlinearity**

The forced association between traditional (conventional) stylistic values and music research assumed from the start “relationship” and “contextuality” as relevant compositional data. We spontaneously constructed scores that included metaphorical instructions for all musicians, or for a specific type of musician. The codification of Lorenzo’s gestures and performative behaviour was the first hint of a nonlinear composition obtained through conduction. The use of improvisation subjected to strict timbral, dynamic, harmonic, rhythmic and metaphorical rules pursued the idea of improvisation as the possibility of applying a contemporary musician’s complexity and compositional ability inside specific macro-semantic grids (1995).

In defining the aggregates that resulted from individual experiments and improvisations, and in stabilising the nature of pre-recorded sample aggregates, the idea of *metacomposition* (the treatment of music aggregates as sonic “elements”) often surfaced. These two approaches shared a need for heterogeneous components to flow inside a composition that can no longer refer to any traditional “ensemble” laws, and that makes use of contextuality, of the fusion between electronic and acoustic bodies, and of the free editing of previous recordings as its main compositional characteristic (in the line of phonographic art).

The fragile harmonic condition of an aggregate inside a metacomposition necessarily meets the need for a nonlinear composition: the possibility for each aggregate and performative context to live within more than one possible musical relationship.

**Nonlinearity.** Multiple solutions for an intentional artwork. Nonlinear instructions. An inter-language theory. Didactic training in our editing and performing languages.

Examples:

- *Partitura viva* (A Living Score). Dancer Raffaella Giordano conducting, 1997. [Read](/projects/files/partitura%20viva.pdf) (PDF)
- *Sempre straniero*. Singer Andrea De Luca conducting, 1998. [Read](/projects/files/sempre%20straniero.pdf) (PDF)
- *Butterfly*. Musician Ikue Mori, conduction, 1998.
- *I cani crocifissi*. Elliott Sharp, conductor; special guest Zeena Parkins.

[Explore the examples](#excerpt)

07.title: Open database
07.markdown:
**Open database**

Interfaces and complexity. We can produce specific sounds and carry out data research for specific environmental needs. We assume that anyone can produce their own music environment digitally: *DJing and home sound processing are everyday music gestures.* Timet organises *access to* and *evident relationships between* a huge number of its own compositional data. Our database is organised to be re-played. We freely provide Timet’s elementary music information to enrich *external* compositional experiences.

The music materials were originally shared under the EFF datashare licence; they are now released under [CC BY-NC 4.0](/open-database/licence).

Examples of open and shared data:

- Timet’s own site: [explore the open database](/open-database).
- Timet’s remix of Mariposa’s recordings: *Metamorfosi di canzoni napoletane*.
- Marco Parente’s website, *Open Songs*. [Explore](http://www.marcoparente.it)
- *Radiotopia*, Ars Electronica 2002, live performance.

[Explore the examples](#excerpt)

08.title: Video experiences and documentary
08.markdown:
**Video experiences and documentary**

Social, artistic and natural organisms meet Timet video projects. Features of a sonic and visual social thought. Examples:

- *Le donne della Valdambra*. Director: Letizia Renzini. [Watch](#video-vald)
- *Stabat basta mater*. Director: Letizia Renzini. [Watch](https://archive.org/download/timet-media-modular/video/stabat%20basta%20mater.mov)
- *L’altopiano*. Director: Stefano Parigi.
- *Trasparente remix* (Pill Scolpisciguerra). Director: Giovanni Antignano. [Watch](#video-scolp)
- *Le tribù di Montevarchi*. Directors: Lorenzo Brusci, Simone Cipolli.
- *Social Forum*. Letizia Renzini, 2002 (not yet available).
- *Dear Giorgio. An evening at the sonic tubular*. Performer: Giorgio Rossi; music and direction: Lorenzo Brusci. [Watch](#video-giorgio)
- *Death in regress*, 1996. Directors: Piero Grazzi and Lorenzo Brusci.

04_2.title: Easy Classics
04_2.markdown:
**EasyClassics, a music animation project**

Featuring Bach, Schumann, Beethoven, Wagner, Ravel, Stravinsky, Ellington, Nono. Interpretations by Brusci (I), Cosottini (I), Roeslmair (D), Gabrielli (I).

Immersive audio installation and concert for laptops, musicians and multichannel sound system.

“…we have been electronically transfiguring pre-recorded classical pieces. They become naturally part of our everyday life, removed from the traditional concert rite: they now live live in a 5.1 public theatre music set…”

Special guests must be requested and scheduled specifically. No audio technical requirements: we use our self-built speakers. Only essential lighting support is needed.

04_3.title: LoLe
04_3.markdown:
**LoLe – Musica leggiadra. Women in an outer world**

Featuring Letizia Renzini and Lorenzo Brusci.

Sound installation and concert for electronics, voice and 8 speakers.

“…Letizia Renzini sings and acts musically inside a widely concrete electronic world. Every vocal narration is a deep concern with women’s social and emotional dimensions of expression.”

Special guests must be requested and scheduled specifically. No technical requirements.

04_4.title: Zarathustra
04_4.markdown:
**Zarathustra, the last animal**

Featuring De Luca, Fiori, Brusci, Gabrielli, Cosottini, Roeslmair, Guerrini.

Sound installation and concert for electronics, three voices, trumpet, saxophone, clarinets, flutes and 4 speakers.

“…Timet has produced a triple CD on *Thus Spoke Zarathustra*, Part I, by F. Nietzsche (reviewed in *The Wire*, April 2003). The concert mediates between the work’s vocation for intimate listening and the need for expression that Nietzsche’s text carries within. Announcement is a fitting metaphor for the concert form.”

No technical requirements.

04_5.title: The poem
04_5.markdown:
**The poem, by Giancarlo Majorino**

Text read live by the poet himself.

Installation and reading for electronics, voices and 8 speakers.

“Lorenzo’s electronics will articulate a sonic environment in which Giancarlo’s words will be mirrored…”

No technical requirements.

04_6.title: Heritage to be played
04_6.markdown:
**Heritage to be played**

Featuring DJ Molly and Lo Pass.

“…playing and processing the music of the twentieth century: new perspectives on live musical interpretation. This is an improvisation: selecting and processing…”

Installation and concert for electronics, turntables, CDJ players, voices and 4 speakers.

No technical requirements.

04_7.title: Compilatione
04_7.markdown:
**Compilatione. A Tuscan electronic scene: classicism meets the beat**

Featuring Leo Cavallo, Dino Bramanti, Andrea Borghi, Mirio Cosottini, Beppe Mangione, Enrico Gabrielli, Mariposa, Paolo Frasconi, Letizia Renzini, Stefano Roeslmair, Lorenzo Brusci, Michele Balduzzi, DJ Seya.

Special guest: Andres Bosshard (“Viking in peace” avatar).

No technical requirements.

04_8.title: Maybe
04_8.markdown:
**Maybe**

*Maybe you would like to be someone else?*

Creative radio mixing of live environments and other music: one night of live and recorded material.

Featuring the Timet Mixing Team (two people minimum).

Please provide technical details about the mixing boards and tools used at the radio station.

04_9.title: AL><Ter
04_9.markdown:
**AL><Ter. A Timet metatheatre experience**

Remixing music events and theatrical pieces: real-time editing of music events, on site or in alternative locations.

Electronics, turntables, CDJ players, voices and 8 speakers.

No technical requirements.

For further details about costs and booking, write to [info@musi-co.com](mailto:info@musi-co.com).

04_10.title: Sampling Art
04_10.markdown:
**Sampling Art. The five recycling totems: a metamusic quintet**

Sampling art by Lorenzo Brusci; five totems by the artists Giampaolo Di Cocco, Filippo Tincolini, Simone Zanaglia and Giacomo Bonciolini. Sound installation.

Sampled composers, among others: F. Zappa, G. Clinton, G. Ligeti, S. Barrett, Bach, L. Berio, N. Cave, A. Artaud, J. Coltrane, Bonporti, G. Petrassi, K. Penderecki, the Beatles, O. Coleman, B. Eno, Pergolesi, Monteverdi.

“…is it possible to give a synthetic and analogue short impression of an entire compositional life? Inside the sonic totems built by our visual collaborators, we place our music meta-bodies, the results of a radical sampling art. We tried out real concentrations of musical experience. The totems are synchronic: they set up a true meta-music quintet…”

No technical requirements.

04_11.title: Shadows
04_11.markdown:
**Shadows**

Freely after *Murder in the Cathedral* (T. S. Eliot). Vocals: Andrea De Luca. Images: Carluccio Rossi. Music by Timet.

Installation and performance for voice, multichannel system and projections.

“…this is a vocal concert. Andrea De Luca is an amazing vocalist: his awareness of ancient music and his command of contemporary vocal techniques give him the ability to apply Eliot’s masterpiece to an electronic world with great pertinence.”

Technical requirements: to be defined specifically for each venue.

04_12.title: May the 1st
04_12.markdown:
**May the 1st. Labour Day: rights and men of the new era**

Featuring Andrea De Luca. Music by Timet.

Installation and performance for voice and electronics.

“No fear. No war. No sorrow. No oblivion. No starvation. No violence. No humiliation. Can music and words be an invitation to a new era of civil involvement? Abstractions and deep reality belong to the same wish: it is possible to build a different awareness of every detail of human life; it is possible to belong to the same world of opportunity, with equal dignity…”

No technical requirements.
